combinations.name: Benzodiazepines
combinations.description: Both slow your breathing, by different routes — the pairing causes a large share of opioid deaths. Tolerance to one gives no protection against the other. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Alcohol
combinations.description: Slowed breathing adds up, and alcohol blunts the reflex that would wake you when breathing drops. A moderate amount of either turns dangerous together. Do not combine.

combinations.name: MAOIs
combinations.description: Opioid–MAOI reactions range from serotonin toxicity to unpredictable sedation and blood-pressure swings. Do not combine.

combinations.name: Gabapentinoids
combinations.description: Gabapentin and pregabalin add their own slowed breathing — a pairing rising in overdose data because each half seems mild alone. If both are prescribed, keep doses low and add no other sedatives.

combinations.name: Other opioids
combinations.description: Same receptor, different names — doses stack directly. A second opioid is a dose increase, not a different drug. Count the total.
